accepted_table_crop_review.notes: The crop holds the whole table from the top rule to the bottom rule; a full-page render of page 13 confirmed this. The printed table has 9 body rows (CSF, Grey Matter, White Matter, Ventricles, Cerebellum, Thalamus, Brain Stem, Average, Time) and 4 value columns (Ours, nnU-Net, PP, dHCP). The row-label column header 'Label' is correctly not attached as a cell. I checked all 36 cells three ways: visually on the crop, on a 300 dpi re-render, and mechanically against a text-layer grid. They all match exactly, including the Time row ('60s', '80s', '> 30min', '> 1h', where '>' is printed). Bold formatting was dropped, which is fine. The same page also has Table 5 (FeTa dataset), and none of its values leaked in; for example, CSF/Ours is 0.923 from Table 4, not Table 5's 0.903. The caption sits below the table and was not absorbed.

The crop holds the whole table, including the FullySup row below the midrule; a full-page render of page 8 confirmed this. The two-level header (Validation set / Test set over DSC (%) and HD95 (pixels)) is correctly flattened as 'top / sub' in all 4 columns. HD95 is printed as HD with a subscript 95, so 'HD95' is a faithful rendering. The row labels keep their citation brackets exactly as printed: Grad-CAM++ [4], Score-CAM [25], Ablation-CAM [17], AMR [16], DRS [9], UM-CAM+SPL (ours), FullySup. All 28 values match the printed text exactly, including the trailing '*' significance markers on the bold UM-CAM+SPL row. The caption's footnote text ('* denotes p-value < 0.05 ...') was not absorbed into any cell.

The crop holds the whole table (5 body rows, header 'Measurement | ICC3 | p-value | CI95%'); a full-page render of page 10 confirmed this. The row labels LCC, HV, bBIP, sBIP and TCD (italic in print) match. The column headers ICC3, p-value and CI95% match; their digits are header text, not missing cells. All 15 values match the printed text exactly, including the scientific-notation p-values (2.60E-05, 2.00E-06, 6.99E-08, 5.02E-12, 7.09E-10) and the bracketed intervals ([0.99, 1.0] and [0.97, 1.0] keep one decimal place, as printed). No caption or body-prose text was absorbed.

I checked all 15 attached cells against the crop, a full-page render and the PDF text layer. Every value matches exactly, including '21-38' (hyphen), '0.5x0.5x0.5' (the PDF uses the letter x, not ×), '[22.6 - 33.4] (28.7±3.5)', '[18-34] (27.3±4.1)' and 'Gholipour et. al, 2017 [14]'. The shape [3, 7] matches the printed table: 3 body rows and 7 columns. Nothing is missing: the Vendor column (General Electric / Siemens; Philips / Siemens) has no digits, so leaving it out is correct. The header 'Image resolution (mm3 )' is the printed 'Image resolution (mm³)' with the superscript flattened. The column is still named correctly, so I did not count it as an error. The two-line row labels 'EVALUATION Quantitative' and 'EVALUATION Qualitative' are joined correctly. No caption text ended up in any cell.

I checked all 35 cells (5 rows x 7 columns) against the crop and the PDF text layer. Every mean±std value matches exactly, including the small subscript std digits. Asterisks are kept as U+2217, which is what the PDF prints, on FetalSynthSeg columns 1, 3, 4 and 7 and on FetalRealSeg column 2. The two-level headers are right: the top level is the testing split (CHUV-MIAL, KISPI-IRTK, KISPI-MIAL) and the sub level is the training split. I confirmed each value column's x-position sits under the right sub-header, and 'Global' spans both header rows. Bold and underline marks are formatting only and are not needed. One aside that does not affect any cell: the JSON 'caption' field is cut off mid-word ('...statistically significantly bet'). The printed caption goes on to say 'better than the second best according to a Wilcoxon rank-sum test (p < 0.05)'.
